answer:
Root cause: the helm client download URL in the `ocp4_workload_showroom` role is dead upstream, not a network problem.

The role composes the URL from two variables in `ansible/roles_ocp_workloads/ocp4_workload_showroom/defaults/main.yml` -- `ocp4_workload_showroom_tools_root_url` (`https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients`) and `ocp4_workload_showroom_helm_version` (`latest`) -- which resolve to `https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/helm/latest/helm-linux-amd64.tar.gz`. That path no longer serves a file, so the request hangs and the task made 10 attempts before giving up with a read timeout.

The mirror itself is serving fine. During the same provision, two other downloads from the same host succeeded minutes earlier: the oc client (`clients/ocp/4.16.9/openshift-client-linux.tar.gz`, 03:12:55) and odo (`clients/odo/v3.15.0/odo-linux-amd64.tar.gz`, 03:15:41). So this is not an outage and not bastion connectivity -- only the helm path is broken.

Root cause category: `dependency`. Confidence: high -- the composed URL is visible in the role defaults, and the two successful downloads from the same host rule out the host-level explanations.

Fix: point `ocp4_workload_showroom_helm_version` at a version the mirror still publishes, or move the download to a source that serves a stable path.
